title_en: 'Ugh, Forget It… I'll Study English and Buy the North American Version' — Japanese GTA 6 Players Hit Out at Gore and Nudity Censorship
summary_en: GTA 6 is finally here, but for players in Japan the experience is looking a bit different. Pre-release concerns about censorship have proven to be founded, with blood, gore, and nudity getting dialed down, but also some more surprising changes.
body_en:
GTA 6 is finally here, but for players in Japan the experience is looking a bit different. Pre-release concerns about censorship have proven to be founded, with blood, gore, and nudity getting dialed down, but also some more surprising changes.
One difference in the Japanese version that’s quickly attracted attention is nudity censorship. But one change in particular is drawing puzzled and disappointed reactions. In most versions of the game, you can see Jason’s naked back and bottom when he takes a shower. However, in the Japanese version, black underwear now mostly covers his butt. Nude beachgoers have also been given underwear.
日本の表現規制のクソっぷりが全世界に知れ渡ってめちゃくちゃ気分が良い
もっと燃やせ
“GTA 6 takes place in such a realistic world, but I hate how this sloppy, out-of-place censorship breaks my immersion.” commented one X user in Japanese. Although Japan has censored full-frontal nudity in games before (such as by adding strategically placed figleaves in Baldur’s Gate 3), a brief glimpse of someone’s bottom has previously been allowed. In Death Stranding, for example, you can see Sam’s bare bottom in the shower, even in the Japanese version.
Japanese news site Game*Spark also spotted some noticeable differences in gore between GTA6’s Japanese and Western releases. In the display settings menu, you can toggle Blood & Gore Intensity on a scale of low to high. The Japanese release completely removes this option. Although bloodstains remain on the ground and on people’s clothing in the Japanese version, there is far less blood compared to Western versions, suggesting that the Japanese version is locked at a lower gore intensity.
However, the Japanese version does still have the option to toggle dismemberment on or off, although it’s toned down compared to GTA 6 in other regions. Japan’s CERO ratings board has previously called on game developers to censor or even remove dismemberment and decapitation in the past. As Game*Spark noted, “Jason wears underwear in the shower but can still blow people’s heads off.”
CERO (Computer Entertainment Rating Organization) is Japan’s age rating board for video games. Although games can be released on digital storefronts with a rating from the IARC instead, a CERO rating is required for 18+ games and physical releases. GTA 6 received a Z (18+) certificate, CERO’s highest rating. To get a CERO rating, a game has to be submitted for review on each of the platforms it will be released on, making the rating process for multiplatform games potentially time consuming and costly (source: Automaton ). If the game fails to pass the first review, the developer must make changes based on CERO’s comments and resubmit. In this case, Jason’s shower underwear might be a result of Rockstar being extra cautious in making sure GTA 6 could get a CERO certification in time for a smooth, worldwide release.
Prior to GTA 6’s launch, fans were already concerned that the Japanese version would be heavily censored. Japan’s PS5 and Xbox store pages only show CERO content warning icons for violence and crime, in contrast to overseas release ratings. Conversely, North America’s ESRB mentions strong sexual content and nudity, among other content warnings.
Other Rockstar games have received similar censorship in Japan. In GTA 5, for example, sex scenes were cut and most of the torture section got axed. Red Dead Redemption 1 and 2 had nudity and sex scenes removed and reduced gory details (especially in RDR2’s American Dreams mission). LA Noire also had nudity censored, with the naked bodies in the homicide cases partially covered by blankets.
Some Japanese users who are unhappy with the censorship have tried downloading overseas versions. However, one big issue is that only the Japanese release offers Japanese language support. “Ugh, forget it… I’ll study English and buy the North American version,” one Japanese user reacted . However, if GTA 6 ever comes to PC, Japanese gamers may get a version that is closer to Western releases, as CERO ratings are not required for PC games.
Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .
Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.
